title: Menu bar title should flash when an existing keyboard shortcut is invoked
line: Using a keyboard shortcut for a menu item now briefly highlights that menu's title in the Global Menu widget, like on macOS.
explanation: Applications export their menus to the Global Menu over the dbusmenu protocol, which has no event for an item triggered by its keyboard shortcut, so the widget could never know which menu was used. The KDE platform theme now watches for shortcut events on actions that live in the exported menu bar and sends a D-Bus signal (org.kde.MenuBar.ShortcutActivated on /MenuBar) with the dbusmenu ids of the item and of the submenu items leading to it. The Global Menu widget listens to that signal from the active window's application, maps the ids to the top-level menu holding the item and shows that title pressed for Kirigami.Units.longDuration (200 ms).

commits.message:
platformtheme: tell the global menu when a menu shortcut is used

Global menus had no way of knowing that an action from the application's
menus was triggered by its keyboard shortcut. When that happens, send a
D-Bus signal with the ids of the item and of the submenus that hold it.

BUG: 481368

applets/appmenu: flash the menu of an item triggered by its shortcut

Using a keyboard shortcut gave no hint in the Global Menu of where that
action lives. Now, when the application reports that a menu item was
triggered by its shortcut, the menu holding it is briefly shown pressed.

BUG: 481368
